title: Primitive recursion: functions built by finite iteration

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems
based_on.pages: 96–104, 106–112 (§§14.1–14.4 and 14.6–14.7; second edition, corrected reprint August 2020)

summary: Build numerical functions from composition and finite iteration, then prove that bounded tests and bounded searches stay within the same class.
abstract: Multiplication can be calculated by repeated addition, and powers by repeated multiplication. Primitive recursion makes this pattern precise: give a starting value and a rule for the next value, then perform the number of steps specified by the input. Starting from zero, successor and input selection, these rules build numerical functions that always return an answer. They also support equality and order tests, finite sums, and searches over a specified finite range. A bounded search reports either its first successful candidate or that the range was exhausted. Explicit constructions, including division with remainder, show how these familiar calculations follow from the same few rules.
